locale: Locale('en'), // buildSubject has no locale parameter

finding.title: Split the 7 tutoring test files that exceed the AG-3 400-line cap

evidence.quote: // L1 widget tests for ManageTutorsScreen (W6.11) — 1619 lines total
// S1 — TutoredWriteRouter unit tests — 1003 lines total
// L1 widget test — InviteTutorScreen — 827 lines total
// L1 widget test — TutorAuditLogScreen — 656 lines total
// L1 widget test for ManageGrantsScreen (W6.12) — 537 lines total
// S2 — Serialization parity tests (Task B). — 523 lines total
// T3 — Read-only surfaces + gating ... — 428 lines total

finding.why: AG-3 caps hand-written Dart files at 400 lines (generated exempt); none of these are generated. No checker for this rule exists anywhere in the repo (grepped Makefiles/tool/ for a 400-line check — zero hits), so it is currently unenforced. manage_tutors_screen_l1_test.dart at 1619 lines is 4x the cap and runs ~10 distinct concerns (loading/error/empty/active-grants/pending-grants/section-headers/per-child-loading/RTL/stale-refresh/multi-child-routing) in one flat void main() with no nested group()s for most of the file — a genuine navigation and merge-conflict cost.
finding.recommendation: Split each file by concern into multiple files in the same directory, or at minimum wrap sections in named group()s; add a Rule-0 line-count check to make audit so new files don't silently cross the cap.
acceptance_criteria: A checker (make audit or a new script) greps lib/ and test/ for hand-written files >400 lines and fails with a file:line-count list
The 7 listed files are each ≤400 lines or split into cohesive sub-400-line files

finding.title: Verify the W7.11 tutor_live_mark_blocked analytics event fires in mark_live_completion_invariant_test.dart
finding.why: The forbidden-write branch deliberately fires an analytics event (W7.11) so tutor-boundary violations are visible in dashboards. The test never passes an AnalyticsService, so _analytics stays null and the `_analytics?.logEvent(...)` call is always a silent no-op — the test cannot distinguish 'analytics fired correctly' from 'analytics wiring is broken.' Repo-wide grep confirms liveMarkBlocked/tutor_live_mark_blocked is referenced nowhere under test/, so this dashboard signal has zero regression coverage.
finding.recommendation: Add a case that injects a hand-written fake or mocktail mock AnalyticsService and asserts logEvent(LogEvents.tutor.liveMarkBlocked) fires exactly once on the tutor-forbidden path and never on the owner/child-self path.
acceptance_criteria: A test in mark_live_completion_invariant_test.dart injects an AnalyticsService fake and verifies logEvent(LogEvents.tutor.liveMarkBlocked) fires on the tutor-forbidden path

finding.title: Replace source-grep assertions with real widget/behavior tests in tutoring WS3.3*/V3C suite
finding.why: All ~65 test() cases across these 9 files import only dart:io + package:test/test.dart, read a lib/ source file with File(...).readAsStringSync(), and assert `contains('<literal>')` — none pump a widget or execute the code they claim to verify. point_config_screen.dart's tutor canEditPoints gate (R1 M1) has ZERO other test anywhere in the repo (verified: no hits in test/features/gamification/ besides this file) — it is the sole safety net for a permission boundary that stops a restricted tutor from editing a child's point configuration. If a future refactor breaks the real `enabled:` wiring while the literal substring survives anywhere else in the ~800-line file (a stale comment, an unreachable branch), all matching tests still pass and the regression ships silently. Conversely, any harmless rename/reformat of the watched code breaks these tests for no behavioral reason. Contrast with test/features/gamification/presentation/screens/reward_configuration_screen_l1_test.dart:615-641, which covers the identical canEditRewards gate with a real testWidgets case that pumps the screen and checks the rendered permission-denied snackbar — proving the correct pattern already exists next door.
finding.recommendation: Convert point_config_screen.dart's canEditPoints assertions (v3c file) to a real testWidgets test mirroring reward_configuration_screen_l1_test.dart:615-641. For the remaining files, promote to real widget/unit tests where the code is reachable from a pumped widget tree; where truly infeasible (e.g. firestore.rules, which has no auth-context mock available), keep the documented-rationale approach already used in w3_41_tutor_security_rules_test.dart's header as the template other files should copy.
acceptance_criteria: point_config_screen.dart's R1 M1 gate has a testWidgets test pumping the real screen with canEditPoints=false that asserts the save affordance is disabled and/or the permission-denied snackbar renders.

A Rule-0 audit grep flags new *_test.dart files under test/ whose only imports are dart:io + package:test/test.dart with no flutter_test/testWidgets usage, outside a documented structural-check exception (as w3_41_tutor_security_rules_test.dart's header documents for itself).
